title: Beta.9 adversarial pack assembled from externally authored public inputs

author.attribution: redact-secret-benchmarks maintainers (assembled by a maintainer-directed agent from externally authored public sources)

implementationExposure.detail: The assembler works inside the project and had read the product contextual-detection spec (placeholder, template and masking rules) before choosing actions. The upstream authors of the excerpted inputs never saw redact-secret; that does not make this pack externally authored, because selection, composition, actions and ranges are the project's.

provenance.construction: No value was generated or altered to look like a live credential. Every credential-like value is a published, non-functional example copied verbatim from an IETF RFC (6749, 6750, 7515, 7519, 7617, 7636, 8959), the AWS CLI documentation, or the detect-secrets and Nosey Parker test suites, whose authors wrote them as fakes. Nosey Parker positive examples of uncertain origin were excluded. Composed fixtures only place those same values into new context. Per-fixture sources are in sources.json.

license.grant: Excerpts keep their upstream licenses: detect-secrets, Nosey Parker and aws-cli under Apache-2.0; the Big List of Naughty Strings and Trojan Source under MIT; RFC examples under the IETF Trust Legal Provisions (code components under BSD-3-Clause). Assembly and compositions are contributed under this repository's MIT license. Attribution: sources.json and README.md.

expectations.authoring: Actions and ranges were authored from each value's published meaning (the RFC or test that defines it) and marked in build-intake.mjs as credential parts; the script converts the marks to UTF-8 byte ranges. No scanner, including redact-secret, Gitleaks, TruffleHog and flare-redact, was run on any fixture before this digest was committed.

fixtures.rationale: RFC 6750 section 2.3: the access_token query value is a bearer token; the host, path and the p=q parameter are not. Source: rfc6750 (verbatim).
RFC 6750 section 2.3: a bearer token in an HTTP request-line query string. Source: rfc6750 (verbatim).
RFC 6749 section 4.2.2: an access token in a URL fragment, with the RFC display line break kept; state, token_type and expires_in are not secrets. Source: rfc6749 (verbatim).
RFC 6749 section 4.1.2: the authorization code is exchangeable for tokens until it expires, so it is redacted; state is not. Source: rfc6749 (verbatim).
RFC 7636 section 4.3 / appendix B: the S256 code_challenge is a public hash sent in the front channel, not a credential. Source: rfc7636 (verbatim).
RFC 7636 appendix B: the code_verifier is the secret that proves possession during the token exchange. Source: rfc7636 (verbatim).

RFC 3986 section 3.1 makes URI schemes case-insensitive, so an upper-case secret-token URI is still the RFC 8959 credential. Source: rfc8959, rfc3986 (composed).
The bare RFC 8959 scheme with no token after it carries no secret. Source: rfc8959 (composed).
Parameter names that extend access_token and refresh_token; their values are a token type and a lifetime, not tokens. Source: rfc6749, rfc6750 (composed).
An access_token name with an extra prefix still holds the RFC 6750 bearer token. Source: rfc6750 (composed).
HTTP field names and auth schemes are case-insensitive (RFC 7617 section 2 via RFC 7235), so a lower-case Basic header is still a credential. Source: rfc7617 (composed).
